- **Note, 2026-11-25 (`KNOTS-WITHIN-REACH-20261125-001`, closed, referee pending).** Answered. The pencil statement holds as argued and checked on 29,599 stages: under parity two loose distinctions are tied or unrelated, so single pairs carry no grading there (under a taking rule a rule among a few loose distinctions does appear, on 1,602 stages). Under not-all-equal the relation between two members' loose distinctions is graded, and not by loose counts alone, but it does not keep the order of the members' steps or arrival delay, from a stage of 7 knots up. So the growing end carries a grading and no distance of its own in the order sense. [Decision](../research/KNOTS-WITHIN-REACH-20261125-001/decision.md).
